Meet our robots Join the team 2005 Competing since 15–30 Student members 10 Awards won FIRST Robotics Competition Team 1661 Griffitrons The Buckley School Since 2005 Sherman Oaks, CA FIRST Robotics Competition Team 1661 Griffitrons The Buckley School Since 2005 Sherman Oaks, CA Who we are About the team Team 1661 is a FIRST Robotics Competition team located at The Buckley School in Sherman Oaks, CA. We’ve been competing in FRC since our team’s inception in 2005 and have won multiple competition awards over the years. Our team typically consists of 15–30 members, and we are working to expand both the team and our efforts to promote STEAM education in our school and local community. We start working in the summer for the spring competition. The team has four areas: Manufacturing, Media, CAD and Programming. d: Join FRC Team 1661 Griffitrons at The Buckley School - no experience required.
k: Our four areas Manufacturing Media CAD Programming Visit us after school
b: Join Join the Team Anyone at Buckley can join. Buckley students only — Team 1661 is open to students of The Buckley School (buckley.org). You don’t need any experience. We usually have 15–30 students on the team and we want more. We start in the summer for the spring competition. Areas Our four areas 01 Manufacturing This team builds the physical robot. 02 Media In charge of promotion and sponsorships. 03 CAD Computer Aided Design. Designs the robot functionality. 04 Programming Works on the coding for the robot. How to join Visit us after school Come by the robotics room any day after school. Buckley students only.

d: Open-source code from FRC Team 1661: robots, vision, dashboards, diagrams and websites.
k: github open source repositories repos

d: Code for our 2026 robot, which won the Creativity Award at the Ventura District event. It is written in Python with RobotPy, a change from the Java we used in earlier years.
k: 1661-RobotCode-2026 Python 2026 REBUILT Python RobotPy Swerve drive Phoenix 6 PathPlanner
b: Swerve drivetrain on CTRE Phoenix 6, with constants generated by Tuner X Shooter subsystem with a flywheel, feeder and screw, all on TalonFX motor controllers with current limits PathPlanner autonomous routines with named commands for the shooter, feeder and intake Field-centric driving, SysId characterization routines and drivetrain telemetry over NetworkTables pyfrc tests that run without a robot

d: Code for our 2025 Reefscape robot. An elevator and a wrist score coral at different heights, a climber handles the endgame, and a swerve drivetrain with Limelight vision drives up and lines up on the reef.
k: 1661-RobotCode-2025 Java 2025 REEFSCAPE Java Swerve drive Phoenix 6 PathPlanner Limelight Elevator
b: Swerve drivetrain on CTRE Phoenix 6 with Tuner X generated constants Elevator, wrist, intake and climber subsystems, with manual, move-to and calibration commands Automatic coral intake and an auto drive, aim and score command PathPlanner autos, including a command that pathfinds, runs a command, then follows a path SysId characterization commands and an autonomous debugger for tuning

d: Code for Eclipse, our 2024 Crescendo robot, which won the Excellence in Engineering Award at the Los Angeles Regional. It shoots game pieces into the speaker, and a four-bar and climber handle the rest.
k: 1661-RobotCode-2024 Java 2024 CRESCENDO Java Swerve drive Phoenix 6 PathPlanner Limelight Shooter
b: Swerve drivetrain on CTRE Phoenix 6 with Tuner X generated constants Shooter, intake, four-bar and climber subsystems, including an assisted far shot Vision subsystem and Limelight helpers PathPlanner autos built from named command pieces, with an autonomous mode selector SysId commands for characterizing the four-bar

d: Code for Nova, our 2023 Charged Up robot, which has a tall chain-driven arm for picking up and placing game pieces. It uses a Swerve Drive Specialties swerve drivetrain.
k: 1661-RobotCode-2023 Java 2023 CHARGED UP Java Swerve drive NavX Arm Autonomous
b: Swerve drivetrain built on the Swerve Drive Specialties library, with a NavX gyro Arm and claw subsystems, plus a game piece mode toggle Several autonomous routines, including placing a cube and then taxiing or balancing A small Xbox controller wrapper and a default drive command

d: Code for Eve, our 2021-22 Rapid React robot, which picks balls up off the floor with rollers. This version is a TimedRobot with one class per mechanism.
k: 1661-Code-2022 Java 2022 RAPID REACT Java TimedRobot PathWeaver Limelight Shooter
b: A TimedRobot that implements a shared Robot_Framework interface for controllers, motors and sensors A class for each mechanism: drive, auto drive, shooter, intake, climb, agitators, Limelight and ultrasonic sensor PathWeaver paths for autonomous

d: A command-based version of our Rapid React code from the 2021-22 season (the repo name predates the season change).
k: 1661-Command-Code-2021 Java 2022 RAPID REACT Java Command-based PathWeaver Shooter Vision
b: Subsystems for the drivetrain, intake, shooter, vertical and horizontal agitators, ultrasonic sensor and vision Commands for intaking and ejecting balls, high and low shots, target finding and teleop driving An autonomous routine and PathWeaver paths

d: Code from our 2020 season. Hop on in and enjoy the ride.
k: shuttle-2020 Java 2020  Java WPILib 2020 Phoenix Elevator
b: Teleop driving and autonomous pieces for driving, the elevator, claws and intake rotation A NetworkTables helper and an echo server Constants for controls, driving, PID and CAN IDs Older mecanum drive code and an alternate control scheme in an extras folder

d: A GRIP and OpenCV pipeline from 2019 that finds reflective vision tape in a camera image.
k: TapeContour C++ 2019  C++ OpenCV GRIP Computer vision
b: Thresholds the image in HSL so only the bright reflective tape remains Finds contours, then drops any smaller than a minimum area Includes the GRIP project file so the pipeline can be tweaked visually

d: A Python tool that generates wiring diagrams for common FRC robot components. The finished diagrams are published as SVG files that any team can use.
k: frc_system_diagrams Python 2025  Python SVG Electronics Diagrams
b: Diagrams are rebuilt automatically when changes are pushed to GitHub Output is SVG, ready to drop into docs Used by the team docs site

d: The source for team1661.com, the site you are on. It is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step, hosted on Netlify.
k: team1661-site HTML 2024  HTML CSS JavaScript Netlify
b: Static pages for robots, awards, sponsors, media and joining the team One page for each of our public code repos, with a search bar A small generator script keeps the code pages and search index up to date Available in English, Spanish and Simplified Chinese, picked automatically from the browser language Dark mode by default, with a toggle for light mode

d: The source for team1661.com/docs, our documentation site. It is built with Quartz and holds notes on electronics and system diagrams.
k: team1661-site-docs TypeScript 2025  Quartz Markdown TypeScript Docs
b: Markdown notes in a content folder, published as a website Pulls in the system diagrams repo as a git submodule Includes a Dockerfile

k: 1661-Dash-2024 JavaScript 2024  JavaScript Electron NetworkTables Dashboard
b: Talks to the robot over NetworkTables Fully customizable with HTML, CSS and JavaScript Supports MJPG camera streams
